shown.chose: could not leave `premise --check` green — it FAILS on pristine v0.25.0 too, so CI on main is red today and was before this work
shown.because: The single gate-grade failure is d-d31f0a5a, whose `chose` records EVICTING src/scene.ts and src/render-scene.ts. Its strong lease therefore names the files the decision deleted, and can never resolve again: a decision that records a deletion is structurally unable to keep its premise. The two remedies the tool prints are both wrong here — `retract` means 'what refuted it' and nothing refuted it (it was carried out), and a replacement decision does not clear the original's lease. Fixing it needs either a premise-side rule that a lease on a path the SAME decision says it deleted is satisfied-by-deletion, or an explicit 'executed' terminal state distinct from retraction. Not mine to invent inside a gate-adoption job. Side effect worth noting: pinning mass-baseline.json cleared one of the 20 ADVISORY missing-address findings (d-cfa92038 named it), so adoption moved the number in the right direction.

shown.chose: could not get the Map's diagram under 7 objects by the region count — hoist draws 9 region boxes and 14 arrows
shown.because: the atlas records 9 distinct from/to regions across 14 crossings (jq -r '.map.crossings.shown[]|.from,.to' | sort -u | wc -l). Any grouping that got it to 7 would have to invent a coarser region taxonomy the atlas never filed, which the brief forbids. What I did instead was hold the TOP-LEVEL object count to 5 per tab (masthead, tab bar, figure, one summary line, one drill strip — counted in-browser by walking the visible children of each section) and make the figure itself teach: layered left-to-right so browser-client -> public-web -> authed-user -> {patient,storage,meter} -> {public-egress,model-provider} reads as a drivetrain in one pass. The honest statement is that the SEVEN rule holds for page objects and does not hold for the diagram's interior, which is a function of the project's own region count.

shown.chose: mutation-check the cli.ts generator-guard line itself for the alias bypass
shown.because: no writing command currently declares an alias — resolve, the only one in the registry, writes nothing — so reverting cli.ts to `c.name === cmd` leaves the suite green no matter what oracle is written. Inventing an alias on a generator purely to make a witness would change the public command surface to test it. Answered by moving the flag read behind commandFor(), which IS mutation-checked (collapse it to a name-only match and the registry oracle reds), and by enumerating the generator-refusal oracle from dispatchTokens() so an alias inherits the demand the day one exists.

shown.chose: could not dogfood either new instrument on the coherence repo itself
shown.because: coherence carries no *.spec.md and no coherence.config.json of its own, so 'verify --fast' here reports 'claims: 0' (an empty cost vector, correctly below the floor and silent) and 'atlas' reports 'no atlas config — nothing to render'. Both features were instead exercised on a purpose-built vitest project with real git history, which is also what discriminated the duration conjecture: cost printed 3.2s over 5 claims with four 800ms report-sourced rows and one 2ms wall-sourced typecheck; atlas printed 'heat █ 75%' for two crossings defined in a file touched by 3 of 4 considered commits, and the panel drew 'energy  cost 3.2s · top 804ms Dogfood  |  heat ██ mintToken 75%'.

shown.chose: batching node:test consumers — no derivable format shipped in v0.17.0, so node:test is RECOGNIZED and refused with instructions rather than guessed at
shown.because: measured on Node 25.2.1: node:test ships NO json reporter (node:test/reporters exports only default, dot, junit, lcov, spec, tap), so there is no report with a vitest-style concatenated fullName to read. Worse, its --test-name-pattern does NOT match a concatenated name — pattern 'outer group inner leaf' matched nothing while 'inner leaf' and 'outer group' each matched — so the vitest mirror (literal substring over fullName) would be WRONG for node:test, not merely unavailable. Parsing tap (nested sub-TAP) or junit (XML) is possible but the matching rule is a second semantic model, and shipping a mirror I have not verified is the one thing this feature is not allowed to do.

shown.chose: did not fix stopReport's 'in this repo' wording, which names the parent's cwd rather than the subagent's working repo
shown.because: it is a real defect (d-a50185c8/d-9ed648e4 has the evidence) but it is outside the task I was given — the command registry — and a hook-message change alters what every agent in every consuming project reads at stop time. That deserves its own pass, with a decision about whether the right fix is wording ('in <repo>' naming the resolved root) or scope (report on the cwd the agent actually worked in, which the hook cannot know). Reproduction: run any subagent whose cwd differs from its parent's; the stop report's counts describe the parent's journal.

shown.chose: verify that agents actually reach for `coherence conjecture` unprompted
shown.because: it needs a real multi-agent fan-out with the instruction line present vs absent, counted over conjecture writes per session. Everything shipped here is mechanism; whether the verb gets USED is a behavioural question this worktree cannot answer. Logged as the open conjecture d-04198572 with its discriminating test.

shown.chose: Scan JSON (package.json/lockfiles/config files) for duplicated domains
shown.because: A live instance sat in this very repo the whole time: package-lock.json said version 0.9.0 while package.json said 0.12.0 -- one fact, two spellings, disagreeing. The detector cannot see it because it reads TS and markdown only. Not built because JSON key sets are dominated by structural vocabulary (dependencies, scripts, name, version) and would need a different rarity model to avoid drowning the report; guessing at one late in the pass would have cost the precision number the whole command is judged on.

shown.chose: A derivable-bound arm: checking a computed statistic against a bound the tool could derive (4,237 removed lines attributed to a 1,139-line file)
shown.because: That is a RUNTIME consistency check over numbers a tool produced, not a static property of source text. It needs an instrumented producer that declares its own bounds (a diff stat cannot exceed the file's line count) -- a different mechanism from anything in this module, closer to a contract on a computation than to duplicate-domain detection. Building a weak static approximation would have made the command mean two unrelated things. Named here so the next agent does not assume 'redundancy' already covers it.

shown.chose: kept the full-tier sub-reading, which had ZERO subjects at the threshold when I wrote it and has one now
shown.because: honest accounting: when I built it hoist sat at 9 commits since lastFullAt against a threshold of 10 — under my own rule that is a mechanism with no subjects and I should have cut it. I kept it on a STRUCTURAL argument rather than a count, and the count has since crossed: hoist is now at 10 and fires. The structural argument is that hoist's habit makes this permanent, not transient — `npm run verify` is `--fast` and `verify:full` is pre-deploy only, so the full tier drifts behind BY DESIGN there, and it is the one case where the section's own stamp reads fresh while every boundary oracle has been skipped. Reporting verify as current on the strength of a run that graded almost nothing is green-by-absence in the newest instrument. A future agent who finds this firing constantly on one project and never elsewhere should re-run: `git rev-list --count --since=<verify.lastFullAt> HEAD` and consider whether the threshold should differ per tier

shown.chose: Re-pin mass and conventions for the control interface: +948 lines, +2 files, +22 symbols, +1 claim, and three new fan-out guards accepted as debt
shown.because: What the new mass BUYS is the elimination of hand-wired lifecycle hooks. Measured today in the consuming project: PostToolUse was bound to one repo-local script on Edit|Write, coherence's own hook was never added, and recordHookReads therefore never ran — so calibrate sat implemented with zero input for the life of the feature and nothing anywhere said so. That is 948 lines to convert a paste-this-block instruction into an installed, canonical, verifiable bundle whose control bit is false when the path is not singular. The three new conventions are guards with fan-out and no contract — isObject (11 sites) is a JSON-shape narrowing used throughout the settings reader, canonicalGroup (3) and canonicalAction (2) classify hook entries during migration. They are pinned as debt rather than converted because a contract for them wants the settings schema to be a declared type, which is a separate change with its own oracle obligation, and doing it inside a release would trade a checked ratchet for an unchecked refactor. Also charted inspectLifecycleHook as project-source to verdict, closing the atlas drift the new self-claim opened
over: Converting isObject/canonicalGroup/canonicalAction into contracts in the same change

It also collapses into the unadopted-gates reading I already declined for being unrepresentable.
